answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full-width 48 px block for all 32 rows. The sampled columns show only thin horizontal 1-row darker lines (rows 6, 14, 19, 23, 27) between bands of similar tone, which gives step or tread texture. No band has a tall vertical face below it, so there is no 3+ row front face. The whole tile is the ramp surface seen from above, descending away from the viewer. The dark 1-2 px columns at the left and right edges from about row 7 down are cut-wall edges, not a receding side face. This is flat terrain with no standing volume.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tan, plank-like ramp made of repeated horizontal bands on a flat dark slate backdrop. It has about 4 lightness steps (light tan, mid, dark seam, shadow), while the paving reference has stones shaded one by one with highlight, mid and dark tones. The measured facts look acceptable (6 visible tones per tile against 3 for grass and 7 for paving, 2% near-flat coverage), but they come from only 7 raw colours per tile and 11 in total. By eye, the bands are uniform with little grain, speckle or per-plank variation, so the surface reads as stripes rather than worked texture. The edge is partly neutral dark (57% near-neutral), so the outline is mixed: a dark line at the top and sides, not clearly a tinted dark-wood tone. The backdrop is a large flat dark area. Overall it is cleaner and flatter than the references and looks more sticker-like. When in doubt, fail.
